title: MP Kanya Vivah Yojana 2026: ₹55,000, Form & Sammelan Date
meta_description: MP Kanya Vivah Yojana pays ₹55,000 for a daughter's wedding via samuhik vivah sammelan. Apply on mpvivahportal.nic.in 15 days before. Full form steps inside.

hero.one_liner: MP pays ₹55,000 for the wedding of daughters from poor families, through samuhik vivah sammelans. Widow remarriage is covered too.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana pays for the wedding of daughters from poor MP families. The state gives ₹55,000 per couple, with ₹49,000 going to the bride and ₹6,000 to the body organising the ceremony.

The catch that surprises families: the money comes only through samuhik vivah sammelans, the mass marriage events organised by panchayats and municipal bodies. A private home wedding does not qualify.

The scheme runs since 2006 under the Social Justice Department and includes Mukhyamantri Nikah Yojana for Muslim couples in the same events. Widows and abandoned women remarrying are explicitly covered.
For a family earning daily wages, a private wedding means a ₹1-2 lakh debt at 3% monthly interest. This scheme replaces that debt with a dignified event and money in the daughter's own account.

eligibility.label: Who qualifies
eligibility.value: Daughters of poor, destitute, or BPL families who are permanent residents of Madhya Pradesh. Widows and abandoned (parityakta) women remarrying are also eligible, with the same amounts and process.

eligibility.label: Age rule
eligibility.value: The bride must be 18 or older and the groom 21 or older on the marriage date. Age proof gets checked against documents, not claims.

eligibility.label: Registration
eligibility.value: The bride's name must be registered on the Samagra portal. The application itself goes on mpvivahportal.nic.in or offline at the local body.

eligibility.label: The event condition
eligibility.value: Marriage must happen in a government-organised samuhik vivah sammelan. Applying at least 15 days before the event date is mandatory.

extra_sections.title: 📌 Sammelan & Amount Status (Verified 31 July 2026)
extra_sections.content:
Sammelan dates are announced district by district on mpvivahportal.nic.in, there is no single statewide date. Apply at least 15 days before your district's event.

The assistance was revised upward to ₹55,000 from the earlier ₹51,000 structure. Some districts deliver part of the bride's share as household samagri rather than full cash, confirm your district's practice at the Janpad or municipal office.

This block updates weekly from official announcements.

extra_sections.heading: The Money, Broken Down
Cash or Samagri: What Actually Reaches the Bride
content: The single biggest confusion in this scheme is the cash-versus-samagri question, and both camps online are partly right. The structure has changed over the years and districts implement it differently.
Older official pages describe household-establishment amounts plus items like utensils and even smartphones. Recent announcements headline ₹55,000 with ₹49,000 as the bride's share.
In practice, many districts hand over a mix: a DBT credit plus a kit at the event, saree, suit fabric, suitcase, and household items. The combined value maps to the sanctioned share.
Before the event, ask the organising office one precise question: how much comes as bank credit and what comes as samagri here. Write down the answer with the officer's name.

The samagri lists themselves are public at the organising office: typically a saree, the groom's suit fabric, a suitcase, utensils, and daily-use items. Checking the list beforehand kills the rumour mill around what you will receive.

extra_sections.heading: The Sammelan Rule: Why a Home Wedding Gets Nothing
content: Families regularly plan a private wedding first and look for the money later, and that order fails. The scheme funds participation in a mass ceremony, not weddings in general.

Sammelans are organised by Janpad Panchayats in rural areas and municipal bodies in cities, typically batching dozens of couples on one date. The event provides the venue, arrangements, and the formal registration.
The design is deliberate: mass events keep costs auditable and kill the dowry-loan spiral that private weddings feed. Your ₹55,000 exists because the format makes it verifiable.
So the correct sequence is: find your district's next sammelan date on the portal, apply 15+ days before it, and plan the wedding for that date.

extra_sections.heading: Documents That Decide Approval
content: Age proof matters most: birth certificate, school leaving certificate, or marksheet showing date of birth for both bride and groom. The 18/21 rule is enforced on paper.
Residence proof of MP for the bride's family, plus the Samagra ID printout. BPL card or income proof establishes the poverty condition where the district asks.
The bride's own bank passbook, Aadhaar-seeded, because ₹49,000 lands there. Open her account before applying, not after selection.
For widow remarriage, the death certificate of the former husband. For abandoned women, the documents the district specifies, usually a legal or panchayat attestation.

extra_sections.heading: The Bride's Bank Account: Set It Up Right
content: The ₹49,000 goes to the bride's own account, not the father's, not a joint one. This trips families where daughters never had their own account.
Open a zero-balance account in her name with Aadhaar before applying. Any bank works, the nearest branch is fine.
Then get NPCI Aadhaar seeding done on it for DBT, which is a separate request from account opening. Say the word NPCI at the counter to avoid the usual KYC confusion.
Post-wedding, that account stays hers. More than one scheme designs it this way on purpose: money that starts a marriage in the woman's name tends to stay under her control.
Carry the passbook's first page to the application, the account number gets copied from it into the form. A single transposed digit there is the most avoidable payment failure in the whole scheme.

extra_sections.heading: What the Groom's Side Should Know
content: The scheme is bride-focused but the groom's family has homework too. His age proof at 21+ gets the same scrutiny as hers, and his Aadhaar goes into the couple's record.
The groom's family bears no application cost and receives no share of the money, that is by design. Their gain is a full wedding event at zero venue and arrangement cost.
Grooms from outside MP are generally fine as long as the bride's family meets the residence condition. Confirm the district's stance when applying, practice can vary at the margins.
One thing his side must accept in writing where asked: the no-dowry declaration. It is part of the event's character, not a formality to argue about.

extra_sections.heading: Why 18 and 21 Are Checked Harder Than Anything Else
content: The age rule doubles as MP's anti-child-marriage checkpoint, which is why verification is strict and document-based. An underage case does not just get rejected, it invites attention.
Acceptable proofs are the birth certificate, school records, or board marksheets. An Aadhaar date alone can be questioned if it conflicts with school records.
Families sometimes discover at verification that a daughter's recorded date of birth differs across documents. Reconcile them at the school or through correction before applying, not at the event.
If the bride turns 18 shortly after the district's sammelan, wait for the next one. Events repeat through the year, and an honest application at the next date beats a doctored one now.

extra_sections.heading: Already Married Privately? Your Honest Options
content: If the wedding already happened at home, this scheme is closed for that marriage, and no agent can reopen it. But the family is not out of options.
First, complete the marriage registration at your local body anyway. The certificate costs little and unlocks every spouse-linked benefit later.
Second, check the bride's eligibility for MP's women-focused schemes that do not depend on the wedding format, like Ladli Behna for married women in the age band.
Third, if a younger daughter's wedding is still ahead, plan hers through the sammelan route from the start. The ₹55,000 saved on her wedding effectively recovers what the first one cost.
The registration office will ask for witnesses and simple proofs of the ceremony, both easy to arrange soon after the event. The same task attempted years later becomes an affidavit chase.

extra_sections.heading: Quick Eligibility Check
qualify: Willing to marry at the samuhik sammelan
disqualify: Private wedding already done or planned outside the sammelan
Family clearly outside the poverty criteria

extra_sections.heading: Status Check and the List
content: After applying, your name appearing in the district's approved list is the real confirmation. Lists get displayed at the Janpad or municipal office and on the portal before each sammelan.
Check the portal with your application number, or ask at the office where you applied. Take the acknowledgement slip they gave you at submission.
Rejections mostly trace to age proof gaps or Samagra mismatches. Both are fixable before the next event, districts hold sammelans through the year.

The payment lands after the marriage is solemnised and registered at the event. If the credit is late beyond a few weeks, the organising body is the follow-up point, with your marriage certificate from the sammelan.

extra_sections.heading: Planning the Actual Day: What the Sammelan Is Like
content: A samuhik sammelan is a full wedding event, not a token ceremony. Stages, pandits and kazis, meals, and dozens of couples marrying with their families present.
The organising body handles the venue and arrangements from its ₹6,000-per-couple share. Your family's job is the guests you bring and the customs you add.

Marriage registration happens on the spot, which quietly solves a problem poor families skip: the legal marriage certificate. That paper later unlocks everything from a spouse's bank nomination to widow pension.
Photos from the event, the certificate, and the acknowledgement slip form your claim file. Keep all three together till the credit lands.

extra_sections.heading: How Districts Schedule Sammelans Through the Year
content: Districts do not run events on one fixed national date. They cluster sammelans around auspicious wedding seasons, typically the winter and spring muhurat windows and around major festivals.
That means missing one event costs you months, not a year. The next date is usually a season away, and the portal lists announcements district by district.
Application volume spikes just before each event, and late files are the first casualties. The 15-day minimum is a floor, applying a month early is the practical standard.
If your district has no announced date, ask the Janpad or municipal welfare branch when the next one is planned. Organising bodies know their calendar before the portal shows it.

Wedding-season months also mean venue and pandit availability drives dates, so announcements can move by a week or two. Treat the portal date as final only when the office confirms it in writing or on the notice board.

extra_sections.text: A wedding should start a household, not a debt. This scheme exists so a daughter's marriage does not cost her family the land.

extra_sections.title: Two Traps to Avoid
extra_sections.content:
Trap one: agents claiming they can get you the money for a completed private wedding. They cannot, the sammelan condition is absolute, and the fee they charge buys nothing.

Trap two: mixing this up with other states' schemes. Bihar and UP run different kanya vivah schemes with different amounts, MP's rules apply only in MP.

extra_sections.heading: The Dowry Angle: What the Scheme Quietly Fights
content: Read the scheme's design closely and a second purpose appears: every rupee flows to the bride's side and the event format leaves no room for dowry negotiation theatre.
Mass ceremonies with official presence make demands harder to stage. Families report that the sammelan format gives them a respectable exit from expectations they could not afford.
The money in the bride's own account continues the same logic after the wedding. It is her working capital for the new household, not a transfer between the two families.
If a groom's side demands payment to agree to the sammelan route, that is dowry by another name. The organising office and the helpline are the right places to say so.

extra_sections.heading: After the Wedding: Papers and Money That Follow
content: The sammelan hands you two assets beyond the ceremony: the marriage certificate and the DBT trail. Store both like property papers.

The certificate is the key to the wife's name change, joint ration card entry, bank nomination, and years later, pension claims. Couples who marry privately often spend months obtaining what this event gives in an hour.
The credit entry of the assistance is proof of the scheme benefit availed. Some later schemes ask whether a marriage grant was taken, answer from the record, not memory.
If the couple moves districts for work, benefits and corrections still route through the district that organised the event. Note its office details before you leave the venue.

faqs.question: Kanya Vivah Yojana MP mein kitna paisa milta hai?
faqs.answer:
Kul ₹55,000 ki sahayata hai. ₹49,000 dulhan ke hisse mein aur ₹6,000 aayojan karne wali sanstha ko jata hai.

Kuch districts mein dulhan ka hissa aanshik roop se samagri ke roop mein milta hai, apne Janpad ya nagar nigam office se district ki practice confirm kar lijiye.

faqs.question: Kya ghar par hui shaadi par paisa milta hai?
faqs.answer:
Nahi. Yeh scheme sirf samuhik vivah sammelan mein hui shaadi par lagoo hoti hai.

Private shaadi karke baad mein apply karne par kuch nahi milta, pehle sammelan date dekhiye, phir shaadi plan kariye.

faqs.question: Sammelan kab hai 2026 mein?
faqs.answer:
Sammelan ki dates har district apni alag announce karta hai, koi ek statewide date nahi hoti. mpvivahportal.nic.in par apne district ki agli date dekhiye.

Event se kam se kam 15 din pehle application zaroori hai.

faqs.question: Form kaise bharein?
faqs.answer:
Online mpvivahportal.nic.in par ya offline apne Gram/Janpad Panchayat (gaon) ya nagar nigam/palika office (sheher) mein prescribed form se.

Dulhan ka Samagra registration pehle se hona chahiye, wahi se application judti hai.

faqs.question: Kya widow remarriage par bhi labh milta hai?
faqs.answer:
Haan, vidhwa aur parityakta (abandoned) mahilaon ka punarvivah is scheme mein explicitly covered hai.

Widow case mein poorv pati ka death certificate lagta hai, baaki process same hai.

faqs.question: Muslim couples ke liye kya vyavastha hai?
faqs.answer:
Mukhyamantri Nikah Yojana isi scheme ka hissa hai. Nikah usi sammelan mein hota hai aur amounts bilkul same hain.

Application ka process bhi same portal aur offices se chalta hai.

faqs.question: List mein naam kaise check karein?
faqs.answer:
Har sammelan se pehle approved couples ki list Janpad ya nagar nigam office aur portal par display hoti hai. Application number ke saath check kariye.

Naam na ho toh wajah puchhiye, zyadatar age proof ya Samagra mismatch hoti hai jo agle event tak theek ho sakti hai.

faqs.question: Paisa shaadi ke kitne din baad aata hai?
faqs.answer:
Sammelan mein shaadi aur registration ke baad DBT se dulhan ke account mein credit hota hai, aam taur par kuch hafton mein.

Zyada der ho toh sammelan ke marriage certificate ke saath aayojan karne wali sanstha se follow-up kariye.

faqs.question: Kya Bihar ya UP ki kanya vivah yojana ka form yahan chalega?
faqs.answer:
Nahi. Bihar aur UP apni alag schemes chalate hain jinke amounts aur rules alag hain.

MP mein sirf MP ki scheme lagoo hai, mpvivahportal.nic.in wala process hi maanya hai.
